items.item: No organizer score exists for any file from this repository. Every number is a HOLDOUT-DTI proxy with known faults as truth.
The competition labels new faults that are not in the public catalogue. Our holdout rewards recovery of mapped faults only (IR-53-03).

H1 (segment-exact learn-predict separation, session-2 rank 1) was pre-registered and REJECTED by its own leakage canary before any holdout run (Exp 4: paired pixel-neighbour AUC 1.000 — label-encoding by construction). It is excluded, not untested. The submitted-candidate lane therefore never used it.

The session-2 candidate was blocked by the literal 3-px overlap flag. Session 3 proved the literal rule unsatisfiable for any nonzero submission (IR-53-26) and released a new candidate under the operative gate (mutual-overlap test, validated against the known duplicate; L-16). The literal flags are still reported unchanged, and the protocol owner has not yet ruled on the interpretation.

Portal [0,1] rejection: the template validator (S7, scripts/validate_submission.py docstring) records a real platform rejection caused by 3,061 NaN px inside the sample's valid region. That cause is owner-documented, not independently verified. Our primary file has no NaN inside the footprint and passes the template validator. A zeros-outside fallback was rejected as non-compliant with 'outside bounds null or nan' (S1).
Data was pulled from a mirror (Dropbox links in the template bridge). Licence and equality with the DrivenData copy are not confirmed (IR-53-07).
The 0.2778 file is not linked to a leaderboard receipt. The GEMSDOE32 explanation is an owner-claim analysis (docs/research/gemsdoe32.md), not a verified result.
Wall-clock time was not logged precisely; the 2-hour guardrail was likely exceeded (disclosed). Exp 2 was re-run once on a corrected footprint (IR-53-05).
Fold CIs use five folds (t, df 4). They are wide (about ±0.007 at q=0.02), so differences of ~0.001 between arms are not resolved.

Protocol deviation: this lane built its own copies of the validator (now deleted, replaced by the template's scripts/validate_submission.py) and of the writer and metric (src/gems53/core.py). The shared template's src/submission_io.py and scripts/validate_submission.py are the reference. Reconciliation of core.py to the template is not finished (remaining work).

Session 2 used 2 of 3 budgeted experiments (E4 canary of H1/H2 and the leak-free audit; E5 holdout of H2 vs bands); E1 and E2 were re-run as reproduction checks; H3 was not run. Session 3 used 3 of 3 (L-14).
No organizer score exists for any file in this repository. Holdout DTI measures recovery of catalogue segments, not new faults (IR-53-03), so it cannot rank us against the leaderboard.

The competition rasters come from a public GitHub mirror (buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE, data/bridge), not from the login-gated DrivenData data tab. Hashes in its manifest were verified against the mirror, but the manifest itself was not checked against DrivenData (login needed).
Session 3 (2026-10-08) used 3 of 3 budgeted experiments: E6 emission-rule sweep, E7 H5 canary + paired holdout, E8 build + gates + publish. H6, H8, H9 and the H7 external-data pipeline were not run.

H7 (radiometric K/eTh alteration index) needs the USGS GeoDAWN radiometric grids, which are NOT in the 19-band stack. Source verified obtainable (S15/S20, CC0) but the ingestion, mosaicking of the four acquisition blocks, and reprojection to the 100 m EPSG:32611 grid were not done (multi-hour task, outside this session's budget).

The operative uniqueness gate (IR-53-26) is a proposed protocol interpretation, not an owner-approved rule change. The literal rule is reported unchanged next to it. Until the owner rules, the 'OK to submit' label on the site rests on the operative gate.

The E6 score-optimum volume q=0.05 (5% of the footprint, 258,369 dots) is REJECTED by the operative uniqueness gate: it is a mutual near-copy (0.872/0.882) of 12GEMSDOE multiphysics. The published volume q=0.0073 (0.73%, 37,722 dots) is chosen among gate-passing volumes; its pooled HOLDOUT-DTI (0.0343) is statistically tied with q=0.01 (0.0379). All volume choices are proxy-optimal only: the holdout truth is the catalogue (IR-53-03), and the registry's high-scoring files sit at 0.7-2% of the footprint.
